q: What does temporal resolution refer to?
options: The number of bands a sensor detects
The precision of a sensor's measurements
The area represented by each pixel
The frequency that a satellite passes over the same location
explain: Temporal resolution refers to the frequency that a satellite passes over the same location.

q: Why does the SkySat constellation have a higher combined revisit rate than an individual SkySat?
options: Individual satellites orbit faster than the constellation
Multiple satellites (6-7 of the 21) pass over the same spot, while a single satellite alone averages 4-5 days
SkySats use a different orbit type than other satellites
The constellation only operates at night
explain: Of the 21 SkySats in orbit, 6-7 pass over the same spot per day as a constellation, while individual satellites average 4-5 days between passes.

q: What three factors does a satellite's temporal resolution depend on?
options: Spectral bands, radiometric bit depth, and sensor type
The speed of the satellite, altitude above Earth, and number of satellites in orbit
Cloud cover, aerosols, and dust
Ground sampling distance, pixel size, and image format
explain: The temporal resolution of a satellite depends on the speed of the satellite, altitude above Earth, and number of satellites in orbit.

q: Which orbit type provides continuous coverage of one fixed area on Earth?
options: Polar orbiting
Geostationary
Sun-synchronous
Molniya
explain: Geostationary satellites orbit the Earth at the same rotation speed as the Earth so the satellite remains fixed over the same spot, providing continuous coverage of one area.

options: The number of bands a sensor can detect
The amount of area on Earth's surface represented by each pixel
The bit depth of an image
The time between satellite passes
explain: The amount of area that a pixel represents is referred to as the ground sampling distance (GSD).

q: A satellite with a smaller GSD value has:
options: Lower spatial resolution
Higher spatial resolution
Higher temporal resolution
Lower radiometric resolution
explain: Smaller GSD values indicate higher spatial resolution because a smaller ground area is represented by each pixel.

q: What is the difference between a wavelength and a band?
options: A wavelength is a specific measurement, while a band is a region of the spectrum where signal strength peaks at a specific wavelength
A wavelength only applies to visible light, while a band applies to all energy
A band is always wider than a wavelength range
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
explain: Wavelengths are specific measurements, such as 450 nm, while bands are regions of the electromagnetic spectrum where the signal strength peaks at a specific wavelength.

q: Which wavelengths make up visible light?
options: Radio and microwaves
Red, green, and blue wavelengths and their combinations
Gamma rays and X-rays
Infrared and ultraviolet
explain: Visible light consists of red, green, and blue wavelengths and their combinations, and is the small section of the electromagnetic spectrum detectable by humans.

options: It absorbs all visible wavelengths equally
It reflects all visible wavelengths equally
It transmits all visible wavelengths
It emits visible light due to its temperature
explain: Snow reflects visible light, which causes it to appear white because all wavelengths are reflected equally.

options: Light is absorbed and converted to heat
Light is reflected back toward its source
Light passing through a material is bent, such as in a prism
Light is emitted due to an object's temperature
explain: Sometimes when light is transmitted through an object, the material bends the light as it passes through, such as in a prism; this is referred to as refraction.

options: The number of bands a sensor detects
The bit depth of the sensor
The frequency of satellite passes
The ground sampling distance
explain: The more bands a sensor detects, the higher the spectral resolution. Some sensors detect just three bands, while others detect hundreds to thousands of bands.

options: The area covered by a single pixel
The precision of the measurement, or how many distinct values can be captured
The number of bands detected
How often a satellite revisits a location
explain: The radiometric resolution of a sensor determines the precision of the measurement.

q: How many values does an 8-bit image contain?
explain: The bit number acts as an exponent to the number two. An 8-bit image would contain 256 values (2^8 = 256).

q: Why can you still get sunburned on a cloudy day?
options: Clouds increase ultraviolet radiation
Ultraviolet light that causes sunburns can pass through clouds
Visible light passes through clouds unchanged
Sunburn is unrelated to light wavelength
explain: Some slightly shorter wavelengths such as near infrared or ultraviolet light can pass through less dense clouds, which is why you can still get sunburn on cloudy days.

q: Besides clouds, what other atmospheric factors can obstruct satellite imagery?
options: Water vapor, dust, and aerosols
Only wind speed
Only temperature
Satellite orbit type
explain: Water vapor, dust, and aerosols can exist in the atmosphere and block or scatter light, in addition to cloud obstruction.
